_about: This agency's AgencyZoom lead sources, in one place: each source name (as AgencyZoom spells it, lower-cased and trimmed) and the group it belongs to, the product each cross-sell source sells, the Role Play backstory a source carries when its group's is not right, and the internet sources Speed to Dial times. lead_sources.py reads it and says what each group MEANS (who the lead is, what to sell, how to work it, Role Play, the money rules) -- the rules stay in code; only this account's names live here. A staff member's name as a source needs no entry: staff.json decides (their own network, or a referral for `referral_source`). 'Name at Company' is a center of influence by pattern. `python3 lead_sources.py --check` validates it; `--discover` lists every source in the saved lead corpus with its group and marks the unclassified; `--write-js` writes site/lead_sources_data.js for the Worker.
groups_note: group keys: cross_sell, existing_new_purchase, generated, winback, referral, personal_network, social_media, center_of_influence, inbound, cold, one_off, commercial, not_a_sale, unclassified

sources._cross_sell: AgencyZoom's own cross-sell labels: the household is already a customer
sources._generated: purchased / generated internet leads (Facebook's are purchased too)
sources._social: Instagram and LinkedIn share AgencyZoom's Social Media category with Facebook but are their own group
sources._found_us: found us -> part of call-in / walk-in (Frank, 2026-09-24)
sources._coi: centers of influence without an 'at Company' in the name (Mariah Serna: Frank, 2026-09-24)
sources._cold: dug out of the system or a one-off list; UTV Expo is an event booth like Crane
sources._commercial: commercial lead generators and lists -> Cerberus; Kraft Lake is AgencyZoom's Commercial Leads category
sources._not_a_sale: BOB: CRM housekeeping for policies not sold. Rewrite: the service department's from 2026-09-24

source_backstory.home no auto: Your home is insured with this agency. Your cars are insured with another company, not this agency. The producer is calling about your auto insurance. You do not need a home quote -- this agency already has your home.
source_backstory.auto no home: Your cars are insured with this agency. Your home is insured with another company, not this agency. The producer is calling about your home insurance. You do not need an auto quote -- this agency already has your cars.
source_backstory.francisco flores: You spoke with Francisco at this agency and he either transferred your call to this producer or passed your information along and told you they would call.

group_who.referral: A customer's referral, or a source named after Francisco Flores: a referral or a warm transfer he handed to the producer.
group_who.inbound: Someone who came to us on their own: called, walked in, or found us on Google or farmers.com (a form Farmers passes on) and asked an agent to contact them. Not purchased.
group_who.cold: Dug out of the system, or a one-off list: Cold lead, FIG QNT (Farmers Quotes Not Taken), Crane Benefit Fair (a booth at a local school fair), Old MVP Leads (the old CRM).
group_who.one_off: Hometown Quotes, X, Other lead. Little volume and no set meaning.
group_who.commercial: Commercial lead generators and lists (Leo, Work Comp, District / Agent Promoter Comm Leads, RCFBH Group Life).

_group_who: this agency's own wording of who a group's leads are, naming its sources, shown to Apollo and on the board over lead_sources.py's plain line
